title: Binary open gluing of sheaf dg objects with compatible target maps
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a topological space with a sheaf $\mathcal S$ of commutative rings, and let $\mathcal C$ be a sheaf dg $\mathcal S$-algebra. Use left dg modules, signed shifts and cones, and the localization $D_X(\mathcal C)$ at underlying quasi-isomorphisms of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Let $U,V\subseteq X$ be open with $X=U\cup V$, and put $T=U\cap V$. Suppose given $L\in D_U(\mathcal C|_U)$, $M\in D_V(\mathcal C|_V)$, and an isomorphism $c:L|_T\xrightarrow{\sim}M|_T$. Then there exist $F\in D_X(\mathcal C)$ and isomorphisms $f:F|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}L$, $g:F|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ satisfying $g|_T=c\circ f|_T$.

Moreover, given any $N\in D_X(\mathcal C)$ and maps $a:L\to N|_U$, $b:M\to N|_V$ satisfying $a|_T=b|_T\circ c$, these objects and isomorphisms can be chosen with a map $d:F\to N$ whose restrictions are $a\circ f$ and $b\circ g$. No quasi-coherence, perfectness, boundedness, or vanishing of negative Ext is assumed. This asserts existence of an actual global derived object and map; it does not assert uniqueness of a morphism from its open restrictions.

source.place: Agent sheaf-dg analogue of Tag 08DG (lemma-glue), including its compatible-target-map clause, and Tag 08BW (lemma-mayer-vietoris-hom). These tags state the ordinary ringed-space versions; the dg versions with the specified action and signed cones are independent obligations, using sdga.tex Tag 0FT5 (definition-derived-category).

proof.text: The existing homotopy-system theorem applies to left modules by the following sign conversion. Form the dg opposite algebra $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, with $a\star b=(-1)^{|a||b|}ba$, and make a left module a right module by $m\cdot a=(-1)^{|a||m|}am$. The two Leibniz formulas agree after substitution; a signed left map of degree $r$ becomes an ordinary right graded-linear map because $(-1)^{|a||m|+r|a|}=(-1)^{|a|(|m|+r)}$. The conversion and its inverse preserve the differential, degree-zero maps, homotopies, underlying cohomology, and the displayed shifts and cones. Thus the homotopy-system theorem gives a triangulated $K_X(\mathcal C)$ and its compatible multiplicative system $W$. Apply triangulated localization to obtain the specified cone triangulation on $D_X(\mathcal C)$. The same argument works on every open subspace. In particular any derived arrow has a distinguished cone triangle; no chain-level representative of the given $c$ is required.

source.place: Tags 0FS7 (proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated), 0FT4 (lemma-qis), 0FT5 (definition-derived-category); derived.tex Tag 05R6 (proposition-construct-localization); explicit left/right sign conversion

proof.text:
Write $u:U\hookrightarrow X$, $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ and $t:T\hookrightarrow X$, and put $P=t_!(L|_T)$ and $B=u_!L\oplus v_!M$. Use the open extension adjunction and its nested-open identifications to define $\alpha:P\to B$ with components adjoint to $1_{L|_T}$ and $-c$, respectively. Choose a distinguished triangle
$$P\xrightarrow{\alpha}B\xrightarrow{q}F\xrightarrow{\delta}P[1].$$
The inclusions of the two summands followed by $q$, restricted to $U$ and $V$ and using $u^*u_!\simeq1$, $v^*v_!\simeq1$, give $i_U:L\to F|_U$ and $i_V:M\to F|_V$. Restriction preserves this triangle by the open-extension calculus. Consecutive arrows compose to zero by the Hom-into-triangle lemma (also on rotations).

source.place: Tag 08DG (lemma-glue), agent dual construction using sdga Tag 0FRW and derived Tag 0146 (lemma-composition-zero)

proof.text: We verify the local isomorphisms by a split-cone calculation, using only triangle exactness. On $U$, let $A=(T\hookrightarrow U)_!(L|_T)$ and let $h:A\to L$ be the adjunction counit. Identify $(T\hookrightarrow U)_!(M|_T)$ with $A$ using $c^{-1}$. The restricted first arrow is then $(h,-1):A\to L\oplus A$. Put $p=(1,h):L\oplus A\to L$. Since $p(h,-1)=0$, Hom-out exactness gives $r:F|_U\to L$ with $rq=p$. Hence $ri_U=1$ and $q\operatorname{in}_A=i_Uh$. The left inverse $-\operatorname{pr}_A$ of $(h,-1)$, together with the zero composition $(h,-1)[1]\delta=0$ in the rotated triangle, gives $\delta=0$. Now $(1-i_Ur)q=0$, so Hom-out exactness in its second clause gives $1-i_Ur=k\delta=0$. Thus $i_U$ is invertible. On $V$, identify the overlap source using $c$ and order the two summands as $M\oplus(T\hookrightarrow V)_!(M|_T)$. The first arrow is $(-h',1)$, where $h'$ is the counit; changing the source by $-1$ reduces it to the same calculation. Thus $i_V$ is invertible. Set $f=i_U^{-1}$ and $g=i_V^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 08DG (lemma-glue), split local triangle; derived.tex Tags 0146 (lemma-composition-zero), 0149 (lemma-representable-homological); explicit dual split-cone calculation

proof.text: Restrict $q\alpha=0$ to $T$. By the unit and counit identifications in the open-extension calculus, its two terms become $i_U|_T$ and $-i_V|_T\circ c$. Therefore $i_U|_T=i_V|_T\circ c$. Inverting $i_U|_T$ and $i_V|_T$ gives exactly $g|_T=c\circ f|_T$. This proves the required transition, rather than just separate local isomorphisms.

For the additional data, let $\widetilde a:u_!L\to N$ and $\widetilde b:v_!M\to N$ be the adjoints of $a$ and $b$, and put $e=(\widetilde a,\widetilde b):B\to N$. By naturality of the adjunction and the nested-open counit compatibility, the adjoint of $e\alpha:t_!(L|_T)\to N$ is $a|_T-b|_T\circ c=0$. Thus $e\alpha=0$ as a global derived arrow. Hom-out exactness supplies $d:F\to N$ with $dq=e$. Restricting this equation and composing with the two summand inclusions gives $d|_U\,i_U=a$ and $d|_V\,i_V=b$, hence $d|_U=af$ and $d|_V=bg$. Without target data the preceding construction already proves the first clause; with target data it uses the very same $F,f,g$. Exactness asserts existence only, so no uniqueness or vanishing of negative Ext has been used.
